questions.question:
By what percent was the price per kilo of chicken increased?
(1) The price per kilo of chicken was increased by P20.
(2) The price per kilo of chicken after the increase was P120.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement (1) gives only the increase amount, not the original price. Statement (2) gives only the final price. Together, we can find original price (120 - 20 = 100) and percent increase (20/100 = 20%). Therefore both together are sufficient. Answer is c.

questions.question:
A real estate broker received a commission of 8% of the selling price of a certain property, what was the selling price of the property?
(1) The selling price minus the real estate agent's commission was P 9 200 000.
(2) The selling price was 250% of the original purchase price of P 4 000 000.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement (1): Selling price minus 8% commission = 92% of selling price = 9,200,000, so selling price can be computed. Statement (2): Selling price = 2.5 × 4,000,000 = 10,000,000. Each alone is sufficient. Answer is d.

questions.question:
Chin-Chin and Queenie May were among those who sold raffle tickets to raise money for the club. If Chin-Chin and Queenie May sold a total of 168 tickets, how many tickets did Chin-Chin sell?
(1) Queenie May sold 60% as many raffle tickets as Chin-Chin.
(2) Queenie May sold 8% of all the raffle tickets sold.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Let C = Chin-Chin, Q = Queenie. Given C+Q=168. Statement (1): Q=0.6C, so we can solve. Statement (2): Q=0.08×Total, but total unknown, so not sufficient. Answer is a.

questions.question:
What is the ratio of m : s : a ?
(1) a = 2, and ms = 64
(2) m/s = 2 and a/s = 1/4

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement (1) gives a=2 but ms=64 has many possibilities (e.g., m=8,s=8 gives ratio 8:8:2=4:4:1; m=4,s=16 gives 4:16:2=2:8:1). Not sufficient. Statement (2): m=2s, a=(1/4)s, so ratio m:s:a = 2s:s:(1/4)s = 8:4:1. Sufficient alone. Answer is b.

questions.question:
If x and y are integers, is x divisible by 17?
(1) The product xy is divisible by 17.
(2) y is not divisible by 17.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement (1): xy divisible by 17 means either x or y is divisible by 17 (since 17 is prime). Alone, not sufficient to say x is divisible. Statement (2): y not divisible by 17 gives no info about x. Together: since y not divisible by 17, x must be divisible by 17. Answer is c.

questions.question:
On Saturday morning the printing machine of Gerpress Printing ran continuously at uniform rate to fill a production order. At what time did it completely fill the order that morning?
(1) The supervisor began the plan for production at 8:08 a.m.
(2) The machine had filled 50% of the order at 9:48 a.m. and 5/6 of the order by 10:18 a.m.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement (1) gives start of planning, not production start. Not sufficient. Statement (2): from 50% to 83.33% (5/6) is 33.33% in 30 minutes, so 100% takes 90 minutes. 50% at 9:48 means completion at 9:48 + 45 min = 10:33 a.m. Sufficient alone. Answer is b.

questions.question:
How many books does Gerard have?
(1) If Gerard had 18 fewer books, he would have only half as many as he actually has.
(2) Gerard has three times as many fiction as non-fiction books.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement (1): Let B = total books. B - 18 = (1/2)B → (1/2)B = 18 → B = 36. Sufficient. Statement (2) gives ratio only, not total. Answer is a.

questions.question:
What number is 24% of x?
(1) 16 is 8% of x.
(2) 1/8 of x is 1600.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: We need the value of 0.24x. Statement (1): 16 = 0.08x → x = 200 → 0.24x = 48. Statement (2): x/8 = 1600 → x = 12800 → 0.24x = 3072. Each gives x, so sufficient alone. Answer is d.

questions.question:
What was the total amount raised for the Payatas Tragedy?
(1) Of the amount donated, 48% came from private corporations.
(2) Of the amount donated, P15M came from personal donations.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Let T = total. Statement (1): corporations = 0.48T, but personal unknown. Not sufficient. Statement (2): personal = 15M, but corporate unknown. Together: personal = T - 0.48T = 0.52T = 15M → T = 15/0.52 ≈ 28.85M. Both together sufficient. Answer is c.

questions.question:
Miriam's total score in the three bowling games was 530. What were her scores?
(1) Miriam's highest score was 198.
(2) The sum of Miriam's two highest scores was 368.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Let scores be a≤b≤c. Given a+b+c=530. Statement (1): c=198 → a+b=332. Not sufficient alone. Statement (2): b+c=368 → a=162. Not sufficient alone. Together: c=198, b=368-198=170, a=162. Both together sufficient. Answer is c.

questions.question:
Is the value of n closer to 48 than to 78?
(1) 78 - n > n - 48
(2) n > 60

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: The midpoint between 48 and 78 is 63. Statement (1): 78-n > n-48 → 126 > 2n → n < 63. So n is closer to 48. Sufficient. Statement (2): n>60 could be 61 (closer to 48) or 70 (closer to 78). Not sufficient. Answer is a.

questions.question:
In last Saturday's Midnight Sale at Sta. Lucia Mall a certain shop sold 75% of the shirts in its inventory. Each shirt was sold for P358. What was the total revenue from the sale of these shirts on that day?
(1) When the shop opened last Saturday, there were 448 shirts in its inventory.
(2) All but 112 of the shop's inventory were sold last Saturday.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement (1): Inventory=448, sold=0.75×448=336, revenue=336×358. Sufficient. Statement (2): "All but 112 sold" means sold = total - 112. Since 75% sold, 25% = 112, so total = 448, sold = 336. Sufficient. Answer is d.

questions.question:
How many more boys than girls are there in the room?
(1) There is a total of 56 girls and boys in the room.
(2) The number of boys in the room equals the square of the number of girls in the room.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Let B=boys, G=girls. Need B-G. Statement (1): B+G=56, not enough. Statement (2): B=G², not enough alone. Together: G²+G=56 → G²+G-56=0 → (G+8)(G-7)=0 → G=7, B=49, B-G=42. Both together sufficient. Answer is c.

questions.question:
In what year was Gerard born?
(1) Gerard's friend Mary Angela, who is 1/2 years younger than him, was born in 1979.
(2) In 1998 Gerard turned 20 years old.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement (1): Mary Angela born 1979, but we don't know if she is 1/2 year younger or older? "younger than him" means Gerard is older. If she is 1/2 year younger, then Gerard born in 1978? But 1/2 year is ambiguous. Statement (2): In 1998 he turned 20 → born 1978. Sufficient alone. Answer is b.

questions.question:
A box contains 48 balls, of which 30 are red and 18 are blue. If 16 of the balls are removed, how many of the balls left in the box are blue?
(1) Of the balls removed, the ratio of the number of red ones to the number of blue ones is 5:3.
(2) Of the first 8 marbles removed, 5 are red.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement (1): Removed 16 balls with ratio red:blue = 5:3 → red=10, blue=6. Blue left = 18-6=12. Sufficient. Statement (2): Only first 8 known, remaining 8 unknown. Not sufficient. Answer is a.

questions.question:
How long did it take Mrs. Alferez to drive non-stop on a trip from her home to Ayala Alabang?
(1) If Mrs. Alferez's average speed for the trip had been 1.5 times as fast, the trip would have taken 2 hours.
(2) Mrs. Alferez's average speed for the trip was 80 km per hour.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Let d = distance, v = speed, t = time. d = vt. Statement (1): d = 1.5v × 2 = 3v → vt = 3v → t = 3 hours. Sufficient alone. Statement (2): v=80, but d and t unknown. Not sufficient. Answer is a.

questions.question:
If Myrna had a dentist's appointment on a certain day, was the appointment on a Friday?
(1) Exactly 64 hours before the appointment, it was Wednesday.
(2) The appointment is between 2:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement (1): 64 hours = 2 days + 16 hours. If 64 hours before appointment was Wednesday, then appointment is Friday at the same time of day as that Wednesday time? Actually 64 hours is 2 days (48h) + 16h. So Wednesday + 2 days = Friday, plus 16h means the appointment is Friday afternoon/evening. But without time range, could be Friday morning? Statement (2) gives time range 2-7pm. Together, confirms appointment is Friday afternoon. Both together sufficient. Answer is c.

questions.question:
What was the average number of kilometers per liter of gasoline a car can consume during a certain trip?
(1) The total cost of the gasoline used by the car for the 640-km trip was P 1 152.
(2) The cost for the gasoline used by the car for the trip was P18.00 per liter.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: We need km per liter = distance / liters. Statement (1): distance=640, total cost=1152, but unknown price per liter. Statement (2): price=18 per liter, but unknown total cost. Together: liters = 1152/18 = 64, km/l = 640/64 = 10. Both together sufficient. Answer is c.

questions.question:
What is the ratio of a to b?
(1) a is 8 more than twice b.
(2) The ratio of a to 4b is 3 : 7.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement (1): a=2b+8, ratio depends on b (e.g., b=1 gives 10:1, b=2 gives 12:2=6:1). Not sufficient. Statement (2): a/(4b)=3/7 → a/b = 12/7. Sufficient alone. Answer is b.

questions.question:
At MSA Tutorial and Review Center, 400 students are enrolled for the Review Program or Academic Advancement Program or both. If 100 of these students are not enrolled in the Review Program, how many of them are enrolled in both MSA Review Program and MSA Academic Advancement Program?
(1) Of the 400 students, 160 are not enrolled in the Academic Advancement Program.
(2) A total of 240 of the students are enrolled in the Academic Advancement Program.

choices.a: Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
choices.b: Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
choices.c: BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement ALONE is sufficient

questions.explanation: Let R=Review only, A=Academic only, B=both. Given R+A+B=400, and not in Review = 100 means A=100. Need B. Statement (1): not in Academic = 160 means R=160 → B = 400-160-100=140. Sufficient. Statement (2): in Academic = 240 means A+B=240 → B=240-100=140. Sufficient. Answer is d.
The pattern is adding 3 each time: 3+3=6, 6+3=9, 9+3=12, 12+3=15, 15+3=18. Answer is b) 18.

questions.explanation: The pattern is skipping one letter each time: C (+2)=E, E (+2)=G, G (+2)=I, I (+2)=K, K (+2)=M. Answer is b) M.

questions.question: I K M O Q ?
questions.explanation: Pattern: I (+2)=K, K (+2)=M, M (+2)=O, O (+2)=Q, Q (+2)=S. Answer is c) S.

questions.question: B D F H J ?
questions.explanation: Pattern: B (+2)=D, D (+2)=F, F (+2)=H, H (+2)=J, J (+2)=L. Answer is a) L.
Differences: +7, +9, +11, next +13 → 37+13=50. Answer is c) 50.
Differences: +13, +15, +17, next +19 → 82+19=101. Answer is d) 101.

questions.question: AB EF IJ MN ?
questions.explanation: Pairs: AB (A=1,B=2), EF (E=5,F=6), IJ (I=9,J=10), MN (M=13,N=14). Next pair should start at Q (17) → QR. Answer is c) QR.

questions.question: ZY WV TS QP ?

questions.question: DC HG LK PO ?

Pairs: (1,2), (5,6), (11,12), (19,20). Differences between pairs: +4, +6, +8, next +10 → 20+10=30? Wait check: 1 to 5 +4, 5 to 11 +6, 11 to 19 +8, next +10 → 19+10=29. Then pair would be (29,30). Next number after 20 is 29. Answer is c) 29.
Two interleaved sequences: odd positions: 4,5,6,7 next 8. Even positions: 9,11,13,15. Next number is 8. Answer is c) 8.

questions.question: A C C F F F ?
questions.explanation: Pattern: A (1 time), C (2 times), F (3 times). Next letter after F is J (F=6, +3? Actually A=1, C=3 (skip B), F=6 (skip D,E), next should be J=10 (skip G,H,I). And appears 4 times. So next is J. Answer is a) J.

questions.question: H H L L P P T T ?
questions.explanation: Pairs: H(8), L(12), P(16), T(20). Difference +4. Next letter after T is X (24). Answer is b) X.

questions.question: E F H G I J ?

Two sequences: odd positions: 6,7,8 next 9. Even positions: 12,11,10. Next is 9. Answer is d) 9.

questions.question: A C F J O ?
questions.explanation: Differences: +2, +3, +4, +5, next +6 → O(15)+6=21 = U. Answer is b) U.

questions.question: B DE GHI ?
questions.explanation: B (1 letter), DE (2 letters), GHI (3 letters), next should be 4 letters starting after I: J,K,L,M. Answer is d) JKLM.

questions.question: A B C D E F ?

questions.question: N O P Q R S ?

Pattern: 29×2=58, then 29, then 29×5=145, then 29, next 29×8=232 (multipliers: 2,5,8 — adding 3 each time). Answer is b) 232.

Differences: +7, +1, +8, +2, next +9 → 332+9=341. Answer is b) 341.

questions.question: F21 H19 K16 O12 T7 ?
questions.explanation: Letters: F(6), H(8), K(11), O(15), T(20). Differences +2,+3,+4,+5 next +6 → 20+6=26 = Z. Numbers: 21,19,16,12,7 differences -2,-3,-4,-5 next -6 → 7-6=1. So Z1. Answer is b) Z1.

questions.question: I18 K16 M14 O12 ?
questions.explanation: Letters: I(9), K(11), M(13), O(15), next Q(17). Numbers: 18,16,14,12, next 10. So Q10. Answer is c) Q10.

questions.explanation: Letters: E(5), G(7), ?(18? No that's number). Pattern: E(5), G(7), I(9), K(11), M(13), next O(15). Numbers: 4,6,?,10,12 — missing 8. So 18? Actually sequence: E4 (5,4), G6 (7,6), ? should be I8 (9,8), then K10 (11,10), M12 (13,12), next O14 (15,14). Answer is a) O14.

questions.explanation: Letters: A(1), C(3), E(5), next G(7). Numbers: 1,3,5,7. So G7. Answer is b) G7.

questions.explanation: Letters: A(1), C(3), F(6), differences +2,+3 next +4 → 6+4=10 = J. Numbers: 26,24,21 differences -2,-3 next -4 → 21-4=17. So J17. Answer is c) J17.

questions.question: J10 L12 N14 ?
questions.explanation: Letters: J(10), L(12), N(14), next P(16). Numbers: 10,12,14,16. So P16. Answer is b) P16.

questions.question: 8R 6T 4V ?
questions.explanation: Numbers: 8,6,4, next 2. Letters: R(18), T(20), V(22), next X(24). So 2X. Answer is d) 2X.

questions.explanation: Letters: J(10), L(12), N(14), next P(16). Numbers: 1017,1215,1413 — first two digits: 10,12,14 next 16; last two: 17,15,13 next 11. So P1611. Answer is b) P1611.

questions.explanation: Pairs: AC (1,3), FH (6,8), KM (11,13). Differences +5 between first letters. Next first letter = 11+5=16 = P, second = 13+5=18 = R. So PR. Answer is c) PR.
